#10773. LEGO is turning a fan-made Interstellar spaceship into an official set

LEGO has officially approved a fan-made Interstellar design, meaning fans will soon be able to build their own version of the iconic spacecraft from Christopher Nolan’s sci-fi movie.

The company announced the winners of its first 2026 LEGO Ideas review on November 9, confirming that an Interstellar project created by user Minibrick41587 will be developed into an official product.

The fan-made design recreates the Ranger spacecraft from the 2014 film and features 561 pieces, along with minifigures of Cooper, played by Matthew McConaughey, and Dr. Amelia Brand, portrayed by Anne Hathaway.

It also includes brick-built versions of the robots TARS and CASE, while the spacecraft itself features an opening rear hatch and interior seating for the two astronauts.

However, this isn’t the first time the creator has attempted to bring Interstellar into the LEGO universe.

Minibrick41587 previously submitted a similar Ranger design that attracted the 10,000 supporters required for LEGO Ideas consideration, but the company ultimately rejected it.

The creator returned with an updated version, which once again reached the required milestone in February 2026. This time, the project was approved.

Interestingly, Minibrick41587 is already responsible for an official LEGO product, having designed the fan concept that became the Polaroid OneStep SX-70 Camera set.

According to IGN, the Interstellar build was one of just three projects approved from 97 submissions in the latest review. The other winners were Tulip Field Windmill and Chinese Cork Carving Art.

Two more designs, based on The Fifth Element and Plants vs. Zombies, remain under consideration.

The announcement follows several other successful fan projects. LEGO previously approved a fan-made Godzilla model, while a Yu-Gi-Oh Exodia design won a LEGO Ideas contest in September 2026.

Fan-made LEGO Exodia wins contest to become first-ever official Yu-Gi-Oh set

New LEGO City Space themed sets revealed: Rockets, Spaceships & more

LEGO’s massive Super Star Destroyer sinks Titanic to become the longest set ever

There’s currently no confirmed release date or price for the Interstellar set. Its 561-piece design could also change before launch, as LEGO’s designers work to turn the fan submission into a finished retail product.

#10771. 6 Email Tools Developers Can Use to Build, Test, and Monitor Better Email

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

A password-reset email can leave your application successfully and still fail the user. It might arrive too late, display an unreadable button, or contain a link pointing to the staging environment.

These failures belong to different parts of the email workflow. Fixing the HTML will not repair authentication, and improving sender reputation will not correct an expired verification token.

For developers and designers, the useful question is therefore: which tool helps us inspect the layer that is failing?

The following six options cover mailbox reputation, local testing, message construction, responsive design, compatibility research, and production monitoring. They serve different purposes; they are not interchangeable alternatives.

For teams managing connected business mailboxes, EmailPond describes a service for automated warmup and reputation monitoring, including connections to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.

The engineering lesson is to distinguish three outcomes:

A successful submission does not establish that a message reached the inbox.

When evaluating mailbox warmup or reputation services, ask what their measurements actually represent. Are they based on participating test accounts, provider feedback, or a proprietary score? What period and sample size do they cover?

Treat any score as one diagnostic input. A result from a testing network is not evidence that every real recipient will receive the same placement.

Also match the tool to your infrastructure. A connected employee mailbox and an application sending through a transactional email provider may use different delivery paths. Activity on one does not demonstrate the health of the other.

Practical exercise: document the sending path for each message type: visible From address, sending provider, authentication domain, and responsible team. This makes later investigations much more precise.

Mailpit runs an SMTP testing server with a web interface and an API for inspecting captured messages. It is useful when testing registration, receipts, invitations, and password resets without delivering development messages to real customers.

Use local capture to inspect more than appearance:

Point the application at SMTP host 127.0.0.1, port 1025, and open http://127.0.0.1:8025 to inspect messages. This example assumes the application runs on the host; an application in another container needs appropriate container networking.

Binding the ports to localhost keeps this development instance off public interfaces. For a repeatable team environment, pin the image to a reviewed version or digest.

Practical exercise: trigger account verification, capture the message, and confirm that the link works once and fails after reuse. Test token behavior through the application, not just by inspecting the email.

Nodemailer provides email-sending functionality for Node.js, including SMTP transport and HTML/plain-text message construction.

Keeping message construction in a dedicated module makes it easier to review and test. Here is a minimal local example using Mailpit:

Run it with node send-test.mjs. Production configuration needs the authentication and TLS settings required by your provider.

SitePoint’s guide to sending email using Node.js provides additional context for building an email workflow.

Practical exercise: move rendering into a separate function and test missing optional fields, long names, and HTML-sensitive characters. Escape untrusted text when inserting it into HTML.

MJML is a markup language that compiles components into responsive email HTML. Its sections, columns, text blocks, and buttons let teams maintain a readable template source.

Keep source templates in version control and compile them during a reproducible build. Review the final output after personalization and any link rewriting.

A component system reduces repetitive layout work, but it does not establish that every message is accessible or renders correctly in every client.

Practical exercise: test a long translated heading, enlarged text, blocked images, and a narrow viewport. The essential message and primary action should remain understandable in each case.

SitePoint’s HTML email design overview offers background on designing within email-client constraints. Pair its established principles with current compatibility data.

Can I Email publishes support information for HTML and CSS across email clients. It helps developers investigate a specific feature before building a template around it.

Start with the clients that matter to your audience. Then inspect support notes for the features your design depends on, including partial support and the date of testing.

A global support percentage cannot tell you whether a feature works for your particular recipients.

For critical content, design a usable fallback. A button should remain identifiable without a decorative background image. A heading should communicate its meaning even when a custom font is unavailable.

Practical exercise: select three visual features in a proposed template and document what users see when each is unsupported. If losing a feature hides the primary action, revise the design.

Compatibility research narrows the risks. Testing the final message in representative clients checks the actual result. SitePoint’s HTML email testing guide provides further background on that review process.

Google Postmaster Tools provides information about email sent to personal Gmail accounts, including authentication, reputation, spam reports, and delivery errors.

Use it alongside application and sending-provider telemetry. Its data concerns Gmail traffic; it is not a universal view of delivery across every mailbox provider.

For example, if delivery errors increase after a provider change, compare the timing with authentication configuration and sending-volume changes. If users report missing messages while the application shows no failures, inspect later delivery events rather than assuming the original SMTP response proves success.

Google’s email sender guidelines explain authentication and sending requirements. SPF authorizes sending infrastructure for the envelope domain, DKIM provides a verifiable signature, and DMARC evaluates alignment with the visible From domain. Configuring them correctly is foundational, but does not guarantee inbox placement.

Practical exercise: create a release checklist that verifies authentication on real test messages from the production sending path, rather than checking DNS records alone.

Tool selection becomes useful when each tool supports a clear acceptance check.

Production systems also need explicit retry behavior. Queueing email can keep slow sending operations out of an HTTP request, but retries can create duplicate messages.

Use a stable application event identifier to track a notification attempt. Where a provider supports idempotency keys, use them according to its documented limits. Otherwise, record provider message identifiers and handle uncertain outcomes carefully: a timeout can occur after the provider has accepted a message.

Test expired notifications as well. A password-reset message delayed in a queue should not promise that its link is still valid.

For delivery-event webhooks, verify authenticity using the provider’s documented mechanism, deduplicate repeated events, and tolerate out-of-order arrival. Avoid logging message bodies or authentication tokens as routine diagnostics.

A useful email workflow gives the team a clear answer to each question: what did we generate, where did we send it, what happened afterward, and could the recipient complete the intended task?

Start with local capture and reliable message construction. Add template and compatibility checks. Then connect production delivery signals to application events.

The measure of success is whether users can verify an account, retrieve a report, or recover access reliably—not simply whether a send function returned successfully.

#10770. Taco Bell quietly tests Fire Piña Hot Dog on exclusive secret menu

Taco Bell has secretly been experimenting with a Fire Piña Hot Dog, and the unusual creation was just one of several bizarre new menu items served at an exclusive event.

The fast-food giant has never been afraid to experiment with unusual food combinations, but its latest creation might be one of its strangest yet.

According to Foodbeast, the chain quietly debuted several never-before-seen dishes during its inaugural Live Más Open celebrity golf tournament on November 2.

Hosted by Kevin Hart at The Ranch at Laguna Beach, California, the event featured celebrities, professional athletes, and creators competing in a nine-hole tournament, complete with an on-course Taco Bell drive-thru serving exclusive food.

Among the new creations was the Fire Piña Hot Dog, which swaps a traditional bun for Taco Bell’s signature chalupa flatbread.

The hot dog comes loaded with pineapple, pickled red onions, cotija cheese, and sauces, combining sweet, spicy, and savory flavors into one rather unexpected Taco Bell creation.

The Fire Piña Hot Dog wasn’t the only surprise. Taco Bell also served Lemon Pepper Ranch Dusted Crispy Chicken Nuggets, a Mini Pimento Cheese Quesarito, and an Avalanche Taco.

Other exclusive dishes included a Baja Caesar Crispy Chicken Crunchwrap and Fiesta Potato Salad.

Foodbeast shared photos of the creations on Instagram, giving fans a closer look at the experimental menu.

Meanwhile, Allrecipes editor Bailey Fink managed to try the Fire Piña Hot Dog and gave it a glowing review, calling it one of the best fast-food hot dogs she’d ever eaten.

Taco Bell is making fans win a golf tournament to bring back a discontinued menu item

Taco Bell launches cake batter-filled Birthday Cake Empanada

Taco Bell combines two fan-favorite menu items in new Cantina Chicken Mexican Pizza

Fink compared its combination of pineapple, cheese, and tangy toppings to a Colombian hot dog, particularly praising Taco Bell’s decision to use its soft chalupa flatbread instead of a traditional bun.

Unfortunately, there’s a catch. None of these experimental creations are currently available at regular Taco Bell restaurants, and the chain has no confirmed plans to release them nationwide.

However, as Dexerto previously reported, the Live Más Open will result in a discontinued Taco Bell menu item returning for a limited time in 2027, with the winning team helping decide what comes back.

Fans will be able to watch the tournament when it premieres on Peacock on November 20.

And while the Fire Piña Hot Dog remains an event exclusive, Taco Bell has a history of turning strange experiments into actual products. Its Baja Blast Pie eventually launched nationwide more than a year after it was first revealed.

#10767. Sony announces new PlayStation Portal with secret features coming in the future

Sony has announced a new version of the PlayStation Portal featuring additional internal storage, teasing future functionality that has yet to be revealed.

The updated handheld, officially called the PlayStation Portal Player Midnight Black, will launch exclusively in Japan on December 10, 2026. While much of its hardware remains unchanged, Sony has confirmed one addition that could expand what the device is capable of.

In its November 9 announcement on the Japanese PlayStation Blog, Sony confirmed that the updated Portal includes additional internal storage intended to support functionality planned for the future.

“Furthermore, with an eye towards future functionality, the new model includes additional internal storage. We will announce details about this feature as soon as they are finalized,” the company said, according to a machine translation.

Sony did not reveal how much storage the updated handheld includes or explain what the additional capacity will eventually be used for.

The announcement has prompted speculation among PlayStation fans about whether the Portal could eventually support downloading games, running entertainment apps, or playing certain titles without an internet connection.

In a discussion on Push Square, one user questioned whether the additional storage could be used for screenshots or save data, while another suggested it might allow the device to run older PlayStation games locally.

Others have suggested that the storage could support streaming services such as Netflix and YouTube, potentially expanding the Portal’s functionality beyond gaming.

PlayStation reveals Midnight black PS5 launching on the same day as GTA 6

Where to buy Sony PlayStation Portal: Price, features, availability and more

Sony drops massive PlayStation Portal update that finally makes it worth buying

However, Sony has not confirmed any of these possibilities, and there is currently no indication that the handheld will support native PS5 game downloads or offline gameplay.

Alongside the storage addition, Sony is dropping the word “Remote” from the device’s official name, changing it from the PlayStation Portal Remote Player to the PlayStation Portal Player.

The company explained that the name change reflects the handheld’s expanded capabilities following the introduction of cloud streaming, rather than a newly announced feature.

Despite the updated name and additional storage, the new model retains its 8-inch LCD display with 1080p resolution and support for 60 frames per second. It also continues to offer haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, and 3D Audio.

The Japan-exclusive handheld will cost 39,980 yen, approximately $250 USD, and includes a one-month PlayStation Plus Premium subscription. Preorders begin November 13, ahead of its December 10 release.

The device is restricted to Japanese-language settings and requires a PlayStation account registered in Japan, meaning players in other regions cannot simply import it for use with their existing accounts.

Sony has not announced plans to release the updated PlayStation Portal internationally or confirmed whether its mysterious future functionality will also become available on existing models.

#10764. 6 Tools for Building Email Automations You Can Test and Debug

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

An email automation can fail even when every service reports success.

These are integration problems. They involve state, timing, retries, and ownership—familiar concerns for anyone building web applications.

This guide uses a hypothetical agency dashboard as a running example. The dashboard manages client workspaces, connects to an email platform, records incoming events, and shows operators whether an action is pending, completed, or blocked.

The six tools below address different parts of that workflow. Each section includes an engineering principle and a practical check to help you apply it.

Postman supports JavaScript assertions against API responses. Use it to establish how an integration behaves before connecting it to a production interface.

A successful request is only one part of the contract. Record response shapes, error formats, pagination behavior, and any documented rate limits.

For an application-owned endpoint that acknowledges queued work with HTTP 202, a post-response test could look like this:

This is an illustrative contract for your application, not a claim about an external provider's response format.

The interface should use the operation identifier to show progress. Displaying “completed” immediately after a 202 response would confuse acceptance with completion.

SitePoint’s introduction to building and testing APIs with Postman provides background on organizing requests and tests. Consult current documentation for the latest interface.

Try this: deliberately submit an invalid request and confirm that the dashboard displays a useful error without exposing credentials or raw internal responses.

The useful engineering question is how your application should represent and control these external operations.

Keep provider-specific calls behind an adapter. Application code might call methods such as pauseCampaign() or listReplies(), while the adapter handles authentication, endpoint paths, pagination, and response normalization.

These are application-defined methods, not an assumed vendor SDK.

Workspace boundaries deserve explicit tests. The documentation distinguishes workspace-specific api-user credentials from broader super-admin behavior. Select credentials deliberately, keep them server-side, and bind every operation to a trusted internal workspace mapping.

For webhook processing, use this sequence:

Confirm the available webhook authentication options before implementation; an HTTPS endpoint alone does not establish who sent a request.

Try this: use synthetic data in two test workspaces and confirm that neither credentials nor resource identifiers allow one workspace to read or modify the other.

Webhooks and workers should be designed for repeated delivery. A sender may retry because your acknowledgment was lost, even when the original event reached your application.

A database can enforce a durable deduplication boundary:

Use a stable provider event identifier when available. If none exists, define an event-specific key carefully. A contact ID alone is insufficient because the same contact can generate many legitimate events.

PostgreSQL's INSERT documentation explains conflict handling. The receiving application can insert an event with:

The placeholders are bound parameters supplied by the database driver. A returned row indicates a new insertion; no returned row means the key already exists.

This protects event storage from duplicates. It does not automatically make every downstream action execute exactly once.

A worker should apply local state changes and mark the event processed in one database transaction. If the action involves another service, record a durable outgoing operation and use the destination's documented idempotency mechanism where available.

Try this: deliver the same event twice, then restart the worker between attempts. Confirm there is one stored event and no repeated business action.

n8n provides error workflows for handling failed executions. This is useful when integrations combine several steps that operators need to inspect.

For example, a reply might require an application status update and a follow-up task for a human reviewer. Decide which step is authoritative and what should happen if only part of the workflow succeeds.

For this agency dashboard, a reply can pause further automated follow-ups until a person reviews the conversation. That is an explicit business rule, not a universal rule for every email system.

Try this: cause a downstream failure after an earlier step succeeds. Verify that recovery resumes safely instead of repeating the entire workflow blindly.

Mailpit supports captured-message inspection and API-based integration testing. Its testing features can also simulate unexpected SMTP responses.

Use it for emails that your application generates, such as workspace invitations or operational alerts. It does not automatically capture messages sent independently by a remote email platform; those need that platform's test facilities and controlled recipients.

For a workspace invitation, test the full path:

Avoid selecting an unfiltered “latest message” in parallel tests. Another test may have generated a newer message, causing a failure—or a misleading pass.

Keep production recipients and credentials out of test environments. Use unique synthetic addresses and test-only tokens.

SitePoint’s guide to sending email with Node.js offers related background on application-generated mail.

Try this: simulate SMTP failure and confirm the application records a pending or failed operation rather than claiming the invitation was delivered.

Playwright can test the dashboard behavior users depend on: submitting an action, observing progress, correcting errors, and inspecting results.

Define visible states before styling the interface. “Request received,” “waiting for provider,” “completed,” and “needs attention” convey different facts.

An illustrative test for a locally running dashboard might be:

This assumes a configured Playwright base URL and an application that implements the illustrated route, labels, and status region. It verifies presentation behavior against a mock response; a separate integration test must verify actual provider completion.

Designers can review these states alongside developers. Use clear text and accessible status announcements, rather than color alone, to communicate progress and errors.

Playwright's visual comparisons can also detect dashboard layout changes. Browser screenshots do not establish how an email renders in Outlook or Gmail.

SitePoint’s guide to testing Node.js APIs with Jest provides a useful companion for checking backend behavior independently of the interface.

Try this: test a slow response, an expired credential, and a completed operation at a narrow viewport. The next available action should remain clear in each state.

Before releasing an integration, demonstrate these properties:

Measure processing delay, retry counts, and unresolved operations. A high volume of successful HTTP requests can hide an accumulating backlog.

Also provide a controlled reconciliation path for missed events. Where the provider supports it, compare local state with the API using a durable cursor or carefully bounded time window. Passing reconciliation results through the same deduplicated processing path makes recovery easier to reason about.

The strongest automation is one the team can inspect and explain. Each tool should help answer a specific question about correctness, failure, or user experience—and every integration should have a tested route back to a known state.

#10763. Rockstar made a real-life GTA 6 Vice City supercar you can actually buy for $1M

Rockstar Games has teamed up with West Coast Customs to bring an iconic GTA 6 supercar into the real world, and fans can actually buy it for a staggering £1 million.

With Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launching on November 19, Rockstar is going all out with its marketing, including a massive takeover of luxury British department store Selfridges.

The collaboration features an exclusive collection of GTA 6 merchandise, but the biggest attraction is a real-life Grotti Cheetah, one of the franchise’s most recognizable sports cars.

Built in collaboration with West Coast Customs, the retro supercar features a striking pink-and-blue paint job inspired by Vice City.

According to Selfridges’ official website, the vehicle is available to purchase for £1 million, putting its price well above $1 million USD.

Interested buyers will need to contact Selfridges Personal Shopping directly rather than simply adding the car to their online shopping cart.

The Grotti Cheetah isn’t just a promotional shell, either. According to Hypebeast, the vehicle features a 4.9-liter naturally aspirated V8 engine, lowered suspension, track-ready tires, and custom-stitched Italian leather upholstery.

It’s also one of six GTA 6 vehicles recreated by West Coast Customs, alongside the Progen Emerus, Invetero Coquette, Albany Buccaneer, Albany Manana, and Pegassi Tempesta.

The car is being showcased at Selfridges’ London location as part of a Vice City-themed pop-up running from November 9 through November 28.

The GTA 6 collection also includes more than 60 products, ranging from Burger Shot uniforms and Vice City sports merchandise to basketballs, hats, and accessories.

Some of the prices are almost as outrageous as the supercar itself. An exclusive Goodtime State Varsity Jacket costs £2,500, approximately $3,355, while a separate GTA 6 varsity jacket is priced at £1,750.

GTA 6 fans say Rockstar’s gifts for influencers are “better” than $400 collector’s edition

GTA 6 collector’s edition confirmed with $400 price tag but no game

New GTA 6 shirt brings Vice City’s 100% completion reward to real life

The expensive merchandise follows Rockstar’s reveal of a $400 GTA 6 Collector’s Edition that doesn’t even include the game.

Demand for official merchandise has already been intense, with some GTA 6 fans reselling promotional items for hundreds of dollars as excitement builds ahead of the game’s release.

Still, the Grotti Cheetah takes things to another level. For anyone who has ever dreamed of owning a car straight out of Vice City, Rockstar has made it possible, provided you’ve got a spare million pounds lying around.

#10761. Call of Duty conversation sparks bomb scare forcing plane and airport terminal to evacuate

A Call of Duty player’s conversation caused a bomb scare at a California airport, forcing passengers to evacuate their plane and part of the terminal before police realized it was all a misunderstanding.

The incident unfolded on Sunday, November 8, at Ontario International Airport in California, where a Frontier Airlines flight was preparing to depart.

According to CBS Los Angeles, a passenger overheard someone discussing a bomb during a FaceTime conversation and immediately alerted the flight crew.

The passenger reportedly heard the words “bomb” and “explosion,” prompting authorities to take the potential threat seriously.

As a precaution, officials evacuated the aircraft and cleared the east wing of Terminal 2 while police investigated the situation.

Police detained the individual responsible for the suspicious comments, but the situation quickly took an unexpected turn.

While being questioned, the passenger explained that the conversation was actually about Call of Duty, with the references to explosives relating to events happening in the video game.

What initially sounded like a potentially dangerous situation turned out to be someone discussing virtual explosions with a friend.

Authorities conducted a sweep of the aircraft but found no explosives or other suspicious devices. Investigators ultimately determined that no crime had been committed.

All passengers, including the individual who had been detained, were eventually allowed to reboard the flight and continue their journey.

It’s unclear how long the evacuation delayed the flight or where the aircraft was headed.

Passengers duct tape angry man to seat after alleged outburst on flight

Family playing Call of Duty too loudly prompts armed police response

Couple gets into viral argument in middle of airport

Surprisingly, this isn’t the first time Call of Duty has caused a police response over misunderstood gameplay.

Back in 2018, a Florida family playing Call of Duty had armed police called to their home after neighbors overheard them shouting about guns and killing each other.

The neighbors believed they were witnessing a domestic violence incident, but officers discovered the family had simply gotten carried away playing the shooter.

Like the airport incident, nobody was charged, and the misunderstanding was resolved without anyone being injured.

Dexerto has reached out to Ontario International Airport for comment.

#10756. Best AI Recruiting Agents in 2026: 6 Compared

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Short answer: Pin (pin.com) covers sourcing through scheduling with approvals you control at every step. Pin says it searches 850M+ profiles and assists recruiters with ranking, outreach, follow-up, scheduling and ATS updates. You approve each step (Assist) or delegate the sequence (Autopilot), and Pin logs every action. Closing and offers stay human.

Be skeptical. Gartner estimated in June 2025 that only about 130 of the thousands of vendors marketing "agentic AI" are real. Test any product on a live role before you pay.

An AI recruiting agent is software that takes a hiring goal, such as "three senior backend engineers in Austin," and works through several steps toward it on its own: finding candidates, ranking them, contacting them, following up and booking interviews. A recruiter sets the brief and the limits and makes the final decisions. The agent assists the recruiter; it does not replace one. See Pin's guide to AI recruiting agents.

It differs from three things sold under the same name:

A quick test: if you stop prompting it, does the search keep moving? If not, it is a tool.

Demand is rising: in Korn Ferry's October 2025 survey of 1,674 talent leaders, 52% plan to add autonomous agents to their teams in 2026.

Compliance. The employer carries the legal duty. New York City's Local Law 144 requires a bias audit within one year before an automated employment decision tool is used, a public summary of results, and candidate notice at least 10 business days before use. The EU AI Act's Annex III classes AI that filters applications or evaluates candidates as high-risk, and the Commission's timeline puts those obligations at December 2, 2027. Ask each vendor whether its ranking is covered, whether a bias audit exists and what logs it keeps. Pin feeds no names, gender or protected characteristics to its AI, uses third-party fairness audits, and lists an Algorithmic Fairness Report (August 2026) in its trust center on request. This is not legal advice.

Pin (pin.com) is an AI recruiting platform with a built-in agent that assists recruiters across the top of the recruiting funnel, from sourcing to interview scheduling.

Sourcing. Pin says it searches 850M+ profiles across multiple sources, including North America and Europe, drawn from professional networks, GitHub, Stack Overflow, open-source contributions, patents, academic publications and the broader web. Start from a plain-language brief, a pasted job description, uploaded ideal résumés or an ATS import. Results arrive as a ranked shortlist, each candidate with a fit score and an AI-written reason. Pin asks clarifying questions about the brief, such as "Is remote considered?" Learn more about AI candidate sourcing.

Assist and Autopilot. In Assist, you delegate tasks one at a time and approve each step. In Autopilot, the agent takes the whole sequence.

In Autopilot, only the email steps send automatically. Pin queues each LinkedIn and SMS step as a task with an AI-drafted message, and the recruiter sends it.

Visibility and learning. Every action appears in a feed, and the agent runs 24/7. Pin's agent page describes an audit log with reasoning, a pause control, approval thresholds for sensitive cases and exclusion lists for past contacts and current employees. The model learns from accept and reject decisions across your team.

Outreach and scheduling. Pin drafts each message from the candidate's profile signals, calibrated to your writing voice. Sequences are multi-channel across email, LinkedIn and SMS: automated email steps plus AI-drafted LinkedIn and SMS tasks in the same sequence. Any reply pauses the sequence, and every channel stays in one thread in a shared team inbox. The Free plan is email-only. Interview scheduling covers time zones, hiring panels and reschedules, with confirmations in your ATS. Pin is rated 4.8/5 on G2. LinkedIn and SMS steps arrive as tasks you send, and closing and offers stay with you. Ask every vendor which steps can run unattended and how you pause them.

Pin offers a free plan, Solo at $99 per month billed annually, Professional at $135 per user per month billed annually, and custom Business pricing.

Do AI recruiting agents have to comply with NYC Local Law 144 or the EU AI Act? Possibly. New York City's law requires a bias audit within one year, public results and 10 business days' candidate notice for covered tools. The EU AI Act treats recruitment AI as high-risk, with obligations scheduled from December 2, 2027. Ask vendors about audits and logs, and consult counsel. #10755. Speedrunners are already breaking Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake with infinite and super jumps

Speedrunners have wasted absolutely no time breaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, discovering glitches that let Link jump infinitely, launch himself into the sky, and skip entire sections of the game.

Nintendo’s Switch 2 remake launched on November 5, bringing a host of improvements to the 1998 classic, including a dedicated jump button that gives players more control over Link’s movement.

As we highlighted in our Ocarina of Time remake review, the new mechanics make exploring Hyrule better than ever.

However, it took speedrunners just a couple of days to discover that Nintendo’s new movement system could be exploited in ways the developers almost certainly never intended.

As reported by Polygon and IGN, one of the biggest discoveries is a technique called “actor jumping,” which allows Link to launch himself absurdly high into the air.

The glitch involves standing on a moving object, such as a Magic Bean platform or movable gravestone, using an item like the Hookshot, and carefully timing the targeting and jump inputs.

When performed correctly, Link goes flying, allowing players to bypass obstacles and reach locations far earlier than intended.

In one demonstration, a speedrunner shows how the technique can be used to access the Shadow Temple shortly after obtaining the Hookshot, allowing players to bypass the Forest, Fire, and Water Temples on their way to the Shadow Temple.

This could allow players to obtain the Hover Boots early, making subsequent sections of the Forest, Fire, and Water Temples easier to navigate.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake review – A masterpiece made better

Ocarina of Time remake launches November 5 with major gameplay changes

Zelda fans obsessed with Dark Link’s “aura farming” in Ocarina of Time remake trailer

And that’s not even the most ridiculous discovery.

このバグ存在しちゃダメでしょｗ慣れると空中で無限にジャンプできちゃうRTAがぶっ壊れるぞコレｗ#NintendoSwitch2#ゼルダの伝説#時のオカリナ pic.twitter.com/WA3kLYgplS

By repeatedly switching between a Deku Stick and another item midair, players can chain jump attacks to keep gaining height, provided Link maintains his upward momentum. The technique also works with Adult Link’s Megaton Hammer.

The timing is extremely precise, and Link must maintain upward momentum, but successfully chaining the inputs allows players to reach areas that would otherwise be inaccessible.

Naturally, all this sequence breaking is causing some hilarious problems.

Speedrunner ZFG has even managed to complete the Shadow Temple as Child Link, triggering an automatic transformation into Adult Link that hilariously distorts his character model during the transition.

We can now beat Shadow Temple as child, which automatically turns you into adult. We still have 1 roadblock to get past before this can be used in a speedrun, but it'll be huge assuming we can get past it. It also looks very funny. pic.twitter.com/s2aoTKCQyY

However, the trick has one major drawback. Completing the Shadow Temple as Child Link transforms him into Adult Link without learning the Song of Time, preventing players from obtaining the Fairy Bow and using the Light Arrows needed to finish the game.

Speedrunners are still searching for a workaround, but with the remake barely days old, players are already finding creative ways to tear Hyrule apart.

Nintendo gave Link a jump button, and speedrunners apparently took that as permission to teach him how to fly.

#10750. Building Location-Aware Interfaces Without Mixing Up Language, Currency, and Region

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

A visitor opens an online store while traveling. Their browser uses English, their account is registered in Canada, their network appears to be in Germany, and their delivery address is in France.

Which currency should the store show? Which products are available? What language should the checkout use?

There is no single answer hidden inside a country code. These decisions depend on different signals and different product rules.

For developers and designers, the challenge is to represent that context explicitly. Otherwise, a convenient shortcut—such as deriving everything from an IP address—can produce confusing prices, unexpected redirects, and incorrect availability.

This article walks through a practical approach to building a regional product interface, with examples that also apply to travel sites, service directories, and applications that retrieve current web information.

Avoid a single variable named country that silently controls every aspect of the interface.

These values can disagree without any of them being wrong.

For an anonymous visitor, network region might help suggest an initial market. Once the user selects a destination, the application should not silently replace it because a later request arrives from a different network.

Write precedence rules for each decision. Language selection and delivery eligibility need separate policies.

SitePoint’s introduction to JavaScript internationalization provides useful background on separating software capabilities from locale-specific adaptation.

This is an illustrative application contract. It keeps the observation's market, currency, and timestamp attached to the value.

Without that context, another component might reuse the amount for a different market or label it as current long after availability changes.

At the API boundary, validate the required fields and their allowed values. A missing amount must not become zero, and a missing availability value must not become “in stock.”

Also define the timestamp precisely. Does it mean the source was fetched, the source published an update, or your database last processed the record? Those are different events.

For the interface, use wording consistent with the evidence: “Checked at 09:00” is more precise than “Live availability” when you only have a timestamped observation.

Browser preferences and network location operate at different layers.

Changing the browser locale can affect language preferences and formatting. It does not relocate the connection seen by the server. Similarly, supplying browser geolocation coordinates does not change the network's public IP address.

This distinction also matters in live-web retrieval. Bixberry describes an opt-in network that routes requests through participants' internet connections. It illustrates how retrieval infrastructure can involve connections outside a conventional data-center environment.

When comparing two responses, record the relevant conditions:

Keep diagnostic records minimal and avoid retaining unnecessary personal information.

For authorized regional testing of your own application, SitePoint’s guide to testing geo-dependent web apps offers related background on separating browser settings from network behavior.

JavaScript's Intl.NumberFormat formats numeric values according to locale and currency settings:

Both calls represent the same euro amount. Formatting it for a different locale does not convert it to another currency.

Do not turn a euro price into a dollar price by changing only the currency argument. A conversion requires a defined exchange-rate source, timestamp, rounding policy, and explanation of whether the result is an estimate or the actual charged amount.

For calculations, choose a representation appropriate to your pricing model rather than relying on floating-point arithmetic throughout. If using integer minor units, remember that currencies do not all use two decimal places.

SitePoint’s overview of the JavaScript Internationalization API explains related formatting capabilities.

Practical check: switch interface language while leaving the selected market unchanged. The number format may change, but the underlying price and currency should remain consistent with the product rules.

A country flag is a weak substitute for a language label. Countries can have multiple languages, and the same language can be used across many countries.

Use clear, separate controls when the product needs them:

Do not expose a control unless its effect is meaningful and implemented consistently. A currency selector that updates a price label but leaves checkout charging behavior unexplained creates confusion.

Before a market change, explain consequential effects. For example:

Changing your delivery country may update availability and delivery options.

Preserve the user's task where possible. If a product is unavailable in the newly selected market, retain its page and show an explanation instead of sending the user to an unrelated homepage.

For designers, test longer translations, currency codes, and expanded validation messages. Use logical CSS properties where appropriate so layouts can adapt to right-to-left content:

These rules are a starting point, not a complete localization solution. Review reading order, icons, numeric content, and translated copy with people familiar with the target language.

A regional interface can behave correctly at the origin and still show incorrect content when a shared cache serves the wrong variant.

If a response varies by market or language, that variation must be reflected in your cache design. One option for public content is an explicit route structure:

These routes are illustrative. They make market and language differences visible, but the rest of the cache configuration must still match the application's behavior.

Personalized prices and account-specific responses require their own cache policy. A public page cache must not expose one account's content to another.

Test the deployed caching layer, not only a local development server:

Keep freshness requirements separate from variant separation. A response can belong to the correct market and still be too old.

Playwright's emulation settings let tests configure locale, time zone, geolocation, and permissions.

This assumes a configured base URL and an application implementing the illustrated route and selectors. It tests the application's handling of explicit market selection under a different locale; it does not prove that the request originated in Germany.

Use controlled API fixtures for predictable frontend tests, then test real routing and caching separately. Browser emulation is one layer of verification, not a substitute for every regional check.

A location-aware application should be able to explain why it chose a language, price, destination, or availability result.

Keep those decisions separate, preserve the context of retrieved data, and make explicit user choices easy to change. Then test the situations where signals disagree.

The result is an interface that works for travelers, multilingual households, remote workers, and anyone whose preferences cannot be reduced to the location of their current internet connection.

It isn’t the first time he has mentioned security concerns or enhancements either.  “We are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. #10743. A Practical Workflow for Testing JavaScript Forms Before Deployment

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Web forms are an essential part of many applications. They allow users to register accounts, submit contact requests, update profiles, and complete purchases. However, a form that appears to work correctly during development can still fail when users enter unexpected values, lose their connection, or submit information multiple times.

Testing forms before deployment helps developers identify these problems early. Instead of relying only on a successful submission, it is useful to test validation, browser behavior, accessibility, and error handling as separate parts of the workflow.

Before writing tests, define what the form should do from the user's perspective. A registration form, for example, might require a valid email address, a password that meets specific rules, and confirmation that the user has accepted the terms.

List the expected outcomes for each field. Consider valid input, empty values, incorrect formats, and unusually long entries. This gives you a clear checklist for testing the form without depending on assumptions about how users will interact with it.

It is also worth considering what happens after submission. Does the form display a confirmation message? Are users informed when something goes wrong? Can they correct their input without entering everything again?

These details help establish the expected behavior before testing begins.

HTML provides several built-in attributes that handle common validation requirements. The required attribute prevents submission when a mandatory field is empty, while type="email" checks whether an email address follows an accepted format.

This approach reduces the amount of JavaScript needed for basic validation. It also provides a useful starting point for testing browser behavior.

However, client-side validation should not be treated as a security measure. Users can bypass browser checks, so the server must validate submitted data independently before processing or storing it.

Developers can also explore SitePoint's HTML and responsive web design guide to understand how form elements fit into layouts across different screen sizes.

JavaScript becomes useful when a form requires custom rules or more detailed feedback. For example, a password field might need to meet a minimum length, or two fields might need to contain matching values.

When testing this logic, check both successful and unsuccessful cases. A common mistake is to test only valid submissions, leaving error conditions unexamined.

Make sure that error messages explain what users need to change. A message such as "Please enter a valid email address" is more useful than a generic notification stating that the submission failed.

Also check that validation does not unexpectedly clear fields or prevent users from correcting mistakes. Error messages should be associated with the relevant inputs so that keyboard and assistive technology users can identify the problem.

Browser developer tools help identify problems that are not immediately visible in the interface. The Console panel can reveal JavaScript errors, while the Network panel helps developers inspect requests sent when a form is submitted.

For example, a form might display a loading indicator but never show a result because its API request returns an error. Inspecting the request status, response, and timing can help distinguish a frontend problem from a backend failure.

The MDN guide to browser developer tools explains how to inspect page elements, debug JavaScript, and investigate browser behavior.

Test situations such as an unavailable server, a delayed response, and invalid server-side data. The interface should communicate the problem clearly and provide a reasonable next step.

A form should remain usable across different devices and input methods. Test it with a keyboard to confirm that users can move between fields, activate buttons, and identify validation errors without a mouse.

Every input should have a clear label. Placeholder text alone is not a reliable replacement because it disappears when users begin typing.

Next, test the form at several viewport widths. Check that labels remain readable, buttons are accessible, and fields do not extend beyond their containers. Long error messages should not overlap other elements or break the page layout.

Automated accessibility checks can identify some issues, but manual testing is still important for understanding the actual user experience.

A simple checklist makes form testing more consistent across projects:

Check server errors and slow network responses.

Confirm that repeated submissions are handled appropriately.

Test keyboard navigation and accessible error messages.

Verify the layout on mobile and desktop screens.

For larger applications, these checks can be supplemented with automated unit and integration tests. Automation is particularly useful when the same validation rules must work consistently across multiple forms.

Reliable form testing involves more than confirming that a submit button works. Developers need to consider validation, server responses, accessibility, responsive layouts, and unexpected user behavior.

By combining HTML validation, targeted JavaScript tests, browser developer tools, and a repeatable checklist, teams can identify problems before deployment. The result is a more dependable interface that helps users complete tasks without unnecessary confusion or frustration.

NASA is hoping to recruit people who could eventually set foot on the Moon, help establish a permanent lunar base, or contribute to future missions to Mars.

“The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars.”

Anyone who believes they have what it takes can submit an application through the official job listing. But before you start packing your bags for space, there are a few boxes you’ll need to tick.

Firstly, applicants must be US citizens and typically need a master’s degree in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) field. However, certain medical qualifications, doctoral studies, and test pilot training can also meet the education requirements.

Candidates also need at least three years of relevant professional experience, although pilots can qualify through specific flight-hour requirements.

#10737. “Endless” cruise ship seized by authorities after passengers abandoned in Cambodia

The Villa Vie Odyssey ship has been seized in Singapore just weeks after passengers were told that the “endless” cruise had come to an abrupt end.

Back on October 27, 200 passengers on board the Villa Vie Odyssey were told they had to get off the ship in Sihanoukville, Cambodia. The operator, Villa Vie Residences, blamed a rise in fuel costs as they were “unable to secure the fuel necessary to continue operations.”

A number of the passengers had sold their homes so they could live on the “endless” cruise, with many expecting the journeys to last for at least 15 years. Other travellers didn’t get to set foot on the ship despite paying for the trip either.

Now, the Villa Vie Odyssey has been placed under a court order in Singapore and seized.

As per the BBC, the reason for the seizure has not been disclosed, but CBS News has reported that it is “likely” from a fuel supplier.

Singapore’s port authority told the BBC that the ship has been “placed under arrest pursuant to a court order,” and that “arrangements for their welfare and wellbeing are being managed by the vessel’s creditors.”

A local law firm, Helmsman LLC, has been named the “arresting solicitor” for the seizure too. Naturally, no passengers are on board the ship, seeing as they got off in Cambodia.

According to the Singapore Courts, the boat was “arrested” on November 8 and remains docked at the Changi General Purpose Anchorage.

A number of passengers still have pieces of personal property onboard the ship after only grabbing the “absolute essentials” upon being kicked off. Randy Cassingham, who has blogged his experiences on the ship, noted that if they had more of a heads-up, arrangements could have been made to protect the property.

#10735. A tiny light trap could unlock million qubit quantum computers

After years of slow progress, researchers may finally be seeing a clear path forward in the quest to build powerful quantum computers. These machines are expected to dramatically shorten the time required for certain calculations, turning problems that would take classical computers thousands of years into tasks that could be completed in hours.

A team led by physicists at Stanford University has developed a new kind of optical cavity that can efficiently capture single photons, the basic particles of light, emitted by individual atoms. Those atoms serve as the core components of a quantum computer because they store qubits, which are the quantum equivalent of the zeros and ones used in traditional computing. For the first time, this approach allows information to be collected from all qubits at once.

Optical Cavities Enable Faster Qubit Readout

In research published in Nature, the team describes a system made up of 40 optical cavities, each holding a single atom qubit, along with a larger prototype that contains more than 500 cavities. The results point to a realistic route toward building quantum computing networks that could one day include as many as a million qubits.

"If we want to make a quantum computer, we need to be able to read information out of the quantum bits very quickly," said Jon Simon, the study's senior author and associate professor of physics and of applied physics in Stanford's School of Humanities and Sciences. "Until now, there hasn't been a practical way to do that at scale because atoms just don't emit light fast enough, and on top of that, they spew it out in all directions. An optical cavity can efficiently guide emitted light toward a particular direction, and now we've found a way to equip each atom in a quantum computer within its own individual cavity."

An optical cavity works by trapping light between two or more reflective surfaces, causing it to bounce back and forth. The effect can be compared to standing between mirrors in a fun house, where reflections seem to stretch endlessly into the distance. In scientific settings, these cavities are far smaller and use repeated passes of a laser beam to extract information from atoms.

Although optical cavities have been studied for decades, they have been difficult to use with atoms because atoms are extremely small and nearly transparent. Getting light to interact with them strongly enough has been a persistent challenge.

Rather than relying on many repeated reflections, the Stanford team introduced microlenses inside each cavity to tightly focus light onto a single atom. Even with fewer light bounces, this method proved more effective at pulling quantum information from the atom.

"We have developed a new type of cavity architecture; it's not just two mirrors anymore," said Adam Shaw, a Stanford Science Fellow and first author on the study. "We hope this will enable us to build dramatically faster, distributed quantum computers that can talk to each other with much faster data rates."

Beyond the Binary Limits of Classical Computing

Conventional computers process information using bits that represent either zero or one. Quantum computers operate using qubits, which are based on the quantum states of tiny particles. A qubit can represent zero, one, or both states at the same time, allowing quantum systems to handle certain calculations far more efficiently than classical machines.

"A classical computer has to churn through possibilities one by one, looking for the correct answer," said Simon. "But a quantum computer acts like noise-canceling headphones that compare combinations of answers, amplifying the right ones while muffling the wrong ones."

Scientists estimate that quantum computers will need millions of qubits to outperform today's most powerful supercomputers. According to Simon, reaching that level will likely require connecting many quantum computers into large networks. The parallel light-based interface demonstrated in this study provides an efficient foundation for scaling up to those sizes.

The researchers showed a working 40-cavity array in the current study, along with a proof-of-concept system containing more than 500 cavities. Their next goal is to expand to tens of thousands. Looking further ahead, the team envisions quantum data centers in which individual quantum computers are linked through cavity-based network interfaces to form full-scale quantum supercomputers.

Broader Scientific and Technological Impact

Significant engineering hurdles remain, but the researchers believe the potential benefits are substantial. Large-scale quantum computers could lead to breakthroughs in materials design and chemical synthesis, including applications related to drug discovery, as well as advances in code breaking.

The ability to efficiently collect light also has implications beyond computing. Cavity arrays could improve biosensing and microscopy, supporting progress in medical and biological research. Quantum networks may even contribute to astronomy by enabling optical telescopes with enhanced resolution, potentially allowing scientists to directly observe planets orbiting stars beyond our solar system.

"As we understand more about how to manipulate light at a single particle level, I think it will transform our ability to see the world," Shaw said.

​​Simon is also the Joan Reinhart Professor of Physics & Applied Physics. Shaw is also a Felix Bloch Fellow and an Urbanek-Chodorow Fellow.

Additional Stanford co-authors include David Schuster, the Joan Reinhart Professor of Applied Physics, and doctoral students Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, and Da-Yeon Koh.

Other co-authors include researchers from Stony Brook University, the University of Chicago, Harvard University, and Montana State University.

This research received support from the National Science Foundation, Air Force Office of Scientific Research, Army Research Office, Hertz Foundation, and the U.S. Department of Defense.

Matt Jaffe of Montana State University and Simon act as consultants to and hold stock options in Atom Computing. Shadmany, Jaffe, Schuster, and Simon, as well as Aishwarya Kumar of Stony Brook, hold a patent on the resonator geometry demonstrated in this work.

#10734. 7 Ways to Keep API Changes Safe as More Teams Join a Project

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

A backend team renames a response field from name to displayName. Its tests pass, the deployment succeeds, and the API continues returning HTTP 200. Minutes later, a dashboard starts showing blank user labels.

The failure is easy to explain: the server changed a contract that another application depended on. Preventing it requires more than asking teams to communicate better. The dependency needs to become visible in documentation, tests, and deployment decisions.

This article follows that field rename through seven practical safeguards. The examples apply to frontend and backend teams working in the same office, across departments, or in different countries.

Start by documenting the existing response and the intended replacement.

The two objects may look equivalent to a person, but software reads specific keys. A client using user.name will not automatically discover displayName.

An OpenAPI description can document request and response shapes alongside status codes and other interface details. Keep it in version control and update it in the same change as the implementation.

Document meaning as well as structure. Does displayName contain user-supplied text? Can it be empty? Is it intended for display only? Must consumers avoid using it as an identifier?

SitePoint’s REST API best practices provides background on interface design. For an existing API, the immediate task is to identify the promises clients already rely on.

An endpoint can serve more than the application shown in the product demo. Consumers may include an administrative dashboard, a mobile app, scheduled exports, internal scripts, and external integrations.

The point is to discover different upgrade timelines. A web application may update quickly, while an installed mobile client remains active for months.

Inspect request telemetry where available, but do not treat a short period of inactivity as proof that a consumer is unused. A quarterly export will not appear in a one-week observation window.

Also record whether consumers reject unknown fields. Adding a response property is often easier to migrate than removing one, but strict decoders can make even additive changes incompatible.

For this example, a transitional response can expose both fields:

Generate both values from the same source so they cannot drift during the migration.

The fourth step needs evidence. The server usually cannot observe which property a client reads after receiving a response. Use consumer version information, published contracts, maintained integration records, and explicit confirmations where appropriate.

For external APIs, removal may require a new version or a documented deprecation process. Do not remove a field simply because the internal dashboard has migrated.

Consider rollback before deployment. If the consumer now requires the new field, rolling the server back to an older response can break it. Either preserve compatibility during rollback or give the consumer a deliberate transition strategy.

A temporary adapter can let a consumer accept both the old and transitional response formats. Keep it narrow and document when it can be removed.

Save the following runnable example as user-label.test.mjs:

Run it with node --test user-label.test.mjs.

The fallback policy is a product decision. For a navigation label, “Unnamed user” may be acceptable. For an operation that requires a verified identity, missing required data may need to stop the workflow.

These tests exercise the adapter only. They do not prove that the live API returns the expected payload or that the application calls the adapter. Add integration coverage at the boundary where the response enters the client.

For UI rendering, insert the returned label as text or use your framework’s normal escaping. The adapter is not an HTML sanitizer.

Several tools can contribute to the review, but their responsibilities differ.

A useful pipeline can lint the API description, compare it against the released baseline, run consumer tests, and verify provider behavior.

Store the baseline deliberately. Comparing two files from the same proposed change can miss a regression against the deployed contract.

SitePoint’s Postman workflow guide explains collections and request organization. Keep shared examples free of production credentials, and include failure responses alongside successful ones.

Mocks should include old, transitional, and new payloads during a migration. This gives frontend developers and designers a way to inspect loading states, missing data, and error handling before the provider rollout finishes.

As more contributors join a project, architectural decisions need to remain understandable outside the meeting where they were made.

Poland has also become a popular choice for companies looking to expand their development teams without limiting their search to local talent.

For a distributed project, the engineering requirement is concrete: a new contributor should be able to identify who owns an interface, which consumers depend on it, and how a change reaches production.

Use actual team names and version identifiers in a real repository. Link the note from the pull request and make unresolved decisions explicit.

A reviewer should not need to infer whether a field is already deprecated or whether the mobile team has been consulted. That context should remain available when colleagues work different schedules.

Define what success looks like before shipping. For this rename, useful checks might include schema-validation failures, client exceptions around user rendering, and unexpected increases in missing-name fallbacks.

Avoid putting names or entire response bodies into diagnostic logs. A template version, consumer version, error category, and correlation identifier may provide sufficient evidence.

Test combinations that can exist during deployment:

Do not assume every combination is supported forever. Define the supported window and its rollback implications.

Once the removal condition is satisfied, retire the old field and temporary adapter through reviewed changes. Update fixtures and documentation so they describe the current contract.

A safe API migration gives teams an explicit sequence, tests the compatibility assumptions, and preserves enough evidence to decide when the transition is complete. That is what allows contributors to work independently without surprising the applications that depend on them.

#10731. Scientists create smart synthetic skin that can hide images and change shape

Synthetic materials are widely used across science, engineering, and industry, but most are designed to perform only a narrow range of tasks. A research team at Penn State set out to change that. Led by Hongtao Sun, assistant professor of industrial and manufacturing engineering (IME), the group developed a new fabrication technique that can produce multifunctional "smart synthetic skin." These adaptable materials can be programmed to perform a wide variety of tasks, including hiding or revealing information, enabling adaptive camouflage, and supporting soft robotic systems.

Using this new approach, the researchers created a programmable smart skin made from hydrogel, a soft, water-rich material. Unlike conventional synthetic materials with fixed behaviors, this smart skin can be tuned to respond in multiple ways. Its appearance, mechanical behavior, surface texture, and ability to change shape can all be adjusted when the material is exposed to external triggers such as heat, solvents, or physical stress.

The findings were published in Nature Communications, where the study was also selected for Editors' Highlights.

Inspired by Octopus Skin and Living Systems

Sun, the project's principal investigator, said the concept was inspired by cephalopods such as octopuses, which can rapidly alter the look and texture of their skin. These animals use such changes to blend into their surroundings or communicate with one another.

"Cephalopods use a complex system of muscles and nerves to exhibit dynamic control over the appearance and texture of their skin," Sun said. "Inspired by these soft organisms, we developed a 4D-printing system to capture that idea in a synthetic, soft material."

Sun also holds affiliations in biomedical engineering, material science and engineering, and the Materials Research Institute at Penn State. He described the process as 4D printing because the printed objects are not static. Instead, they can actively change in response to environmental conditions.

Printing Digital Instructions Into Material

To achieve this adaptability, the team used a method called halftone-encoded printing. This technique converts image or texture data into binary ones and zeros and embeds that information directly into the material. The approach is similar to how dot patterns are used in newspapers or photographs to create images.

By encoding these digital patterns within the hydrogel, the researchers can program how the smart skin reacts to different stimuli. The printed patterns determine how various regions of the material respond. Some areas may swell, shrink, or soften more than others when exposed to temperature changes, liquids, or mechanical forces. By carefully designing these patterns, the team can control the material's overall behavior.

"In simple terms, we're printing instructions into the material," Sun explained. "Those instructions tell the skin how to react when something changes around it."

One of the most eye-catching demonstrations involved the material's ability to conceal and reveal visual information. Haoqing Yang, a doctoral candidate in IME and the paper's first author, said this capability highlights the potential of the smart skin.

To demonstrate the effect, the team encoded an image of the Mona Lisa into the hydrogel film. When the material was washed with ethanol, it appeared transparent and showed no visible image. The hidden image became clear only after the film was placed in ice water or gradually heated.

Yang noted that the Mona Lisa was used only as an example. The printing technique allows virtually any image to be encoded into the hydrogel.

"This behavior could be used for camouflage, where a surface blends into its environment, or for information encryption, where messages are hidden and only revealed under specific conditions," Yang said.

The researchers also showed that concealed patterns could be detected by gently stretching the material and analyzing how it deforms using digital image correlation analysis. This means information can be revealed not only visually, but also through mechanical interaction, adding an extra level of security.

The smart skin also demonstrated remarkable flexibility. According to Sun, the material can easily shift from a flat sheet into complex, bio-inspired shapes with detailed surface textures. Unlike many other shape-changing materials, this transformation does not require multiple layers or different substances.

Instead, the changes in shape and texture are controlled entirely by the digitally printed halftone patterns within a single sheet. This allows the material to replicate effects similar to those seen in cephalopod skin.

Building on this capability, the team showed that multiple functions can be programmed to work together. By carefully designing the halftone patterns, they encoded the Mona Lisa image into flat films that later transformed into three-dimensional forms. As the sheets curved into dome-like shapes, the hidden image slowly appeared, showing that changes in shape and visual appearance can be coordinated within one material.

"Similar to how cephalopods coordinate body shape and skin patterning, the synthetic smart skin can simultaneously control what it looks like and how it deforms, all within a single, soft material," Sun said.

Expanding the Potential of 4D-Printed Hydrogels

Sun said the new work builds on earlier research by the team on 4D-printed smart hydrogels, which was also published in Nature Communications. That earlier study focused on combining mechanical properties with programmable transitions from flat to three-dimensional forms. In the current research, the team expanded the approach by using halftone-encoded 4D printing to integrate even more functions into a single hydrogel film.

Looking ahead, the researchers aim to create a scalable and versatile platform that allows precise digital encoding of multiple functions within one adaptive material.

"This interdisciplinary research at the intersection of advanced manufacturing, intelligent materials and mechanics opens new opportunities with broad implications for stimulus-responsive systems, biomimetic engineering, advanced encryption technologies, biomedical devices and more," Sun said.

The study also included Penn State co-authors Haotian Li and Juchen Zhang, both doctoral candidates in IME, and Tengxiao Liu, a lecturer in biomedical engineering. H. Jerry Qi, professor of mechanical engineering at Georgia Institute of Technology, also collaborated on the project.

#10730. Nintendo is hiring someone to preserve its old games and consoles

Nintendo is looking to hire someone to help preserve its gaming history, as more and more classic titles risk being lost to time.

Video game preservation has become an increasingly important issue, especially as older consoles become obsolete and digital storefronts shut down. With many games never receiving modern re-releases, some are becoming virtually impossible to play without tracking down their original hardware.

In fact, a 2023 study found that 87% of classic games released in the US were no longer commercially available.

Now, Nintendo is taking steps to ensure that important parts of its own gaming history are preserved for future generations.

According to its official job listing, the company is searching for a Digital Archivist, who will help preserve technical records and development materials from previous generations.

“We are seeking a Digital Archivist, Historical Systems to support the preservation, organization, and accessibility of historical hardware and software information,” the description reads.

The successful applicant will be responsible for organizing historical documents, creating a searchable database, and interviewing long-serving employees to record their knowledge.

Nintendo says the goal is to ensure information about its older hardware and software remains accessible to its engineering, development, and research teams.

The position is based in Redmond, Washington, and pays between $35 and $55 per hour on a 12-month contract. Applicants need a relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, alongside at least two years working in areas such as digital archiving or records management.

However, while the move could help safeguard Nintendo’s history, it doesn’t necessarily mean that more classic games will become available to players.
